title: Licensing and support
desc: How tech vendors sell: licences, support, partners, lifecycle

src.l: HPE Networking end of life information

pages.h: Buy once or pay as you go
pages.t: A perpetual licence is bought once and used for a particular version of the software with no end date. A subscription is paid for a period, such as a year, and stops when you stop paying.
g: Permission from the vendor to use software, under set conditions.

pages.t: Subscriptions give the vendor recurring revenue and let the customer start with a lower upfront cost. They usually include updates and fixes while active. The trade-off for the customer is a continuing cost.
g: Income that repeats every month or year.
What you pay at the start.

pages.t: Always ask: is this hardware only, a one-off licence, or a subscription? Many products mix them: you buy the box once and subscribe to security updates or cloud features. What stops when a subscription ends differs by vendor: sometimes only updates and features, sometimes the device itself.
g: A physical device with no extra software fees.

quiz.q: What defines a subscription licence?
o: It is paid for a period and ends if not renewed
quiz.w: Subscriptions are temporary and billed per period.

quiz.q: What is a common benefit of subscriptions for the customer?
quiz.w: Temporary licences lower the initial cost, at the price of ongoing payments.

quiz.q: A customer's subscription is about to end. What should you check?
o: Nothing, the device always keeps working as before
What stops: it differs by vendor, from updates and features to the device itself
Whether the box can be returned
quiz.w: Some vendors stop only updates and cloud features, while others shut the device down after a grace period.

pages.t: The vendor makes the product. A distributor buys in volume, holds stock and sells to resellers. Resellers sell to the end customer. Wholesalers like distributors do not sell directly to the public.
g: The company that makes or owns the product brand.
The route from vendor to end customer through partners.

pages.t: A value-added reseller (VAR) adds something to the product: integration, consulting, training or a tailored solution. A system integrator combines products from many vendors into one working solution for a customer.
g: Value-added reseller: sells a product plus its own added services.
Builds one working solution out of many parts.

pages.t: An MSP takes ongoing responsibility for a customer's IT, often for a fixed monthly fee, instead of fixing things only when they break. MSPs like subscriptions and cloud-managed products that they can monitor remotely.
g: Managed service provider: runs a customer's IT for a recurring fee.
Paying for help only when something breaks.

quiz.q: Who buys from the vendor in volume and sells to resellers?
quiz.w: Distributors hold stock and serve resellers.

quiz.q: What makes a VAR 'value-added'?
o: Services or features added on top of the product
It is run by the vendor
quiz.w: A VAR adds integration, consulting, training or a tailored solution.

quiz.q: Which partner type prefers products it can monitor remotely for a monthly fee?
quiz.w: MSPs run IT as an ongoing subscription service.

lessons.title: Per device, per user, per feature

src.l: RWTH IT Center: basics of licensing

pages.t: A licence counts something. Per device: each firewall, camera or access point. Per user: each person using the service. Per feature: some vendors charge extra to unlock extras such as advanced security. Some licences count simultaneous users instead of named people.
g: The thing a licence is counted by.

pages.t: The metric decides how a customer's cost grows. A per-device licence grows with every new box. A per-user one grows with staff. A customer with few users but many devices may find per-user cheaper, and the other way round, so compare the actual terms.
g: To grow in size, such as more sites or staff.

pages.t: Before quoting, check what is counted, what the licence includes, and how long it runs. Vendors use different words for similar things, so read the licence description or ask your contact. Never assume that 'one licence' covers the whole site.
g: The vendor's document saying what a licence covers.

quiz.q: What is a per-user licence counted by?
o: The number of people using it
quiz.w: Per-user licences scale with the number of users.

quiz.q: A customer with 3 staff adds 10 more cameras. Which kind of licence cost grows?
quiz.w: A per-device licence grows with every new device, while a per-user one follows the number of people.

quiz.q: What should you do before quoting a licence?
o: Check what it counts and what it includes
quiz.w: Metrics and inclusions vary between vendors.

pages.t: A warranty is the vendor's promise that a product is free from defects for a set time, often limited in duration or scope. It usually covers faults in materials and workmanship, not misuse or wear.
g: A fault in the product from how it was made.
A warranty restricted in time, scope or both.

pages.t: A support contract goes beyond the warranty: access to technical help, software updates and often hardware replacement. Vendors sell tiers, from basic to premium, differing in help hours and replacement speed.
g: A level of service, such as standard or premium.
Technical assistance centre: the vendor's help desk.

pages.t: Ask what the base warranty is, what tiers exist, and when the support clock starts. Higher tiers often add faster hardware replacement and longer or 24x7 help. Customers with critical systems should consider them, while others may not need more than the standard.

quiz.q: What does a standard warranty typically cover?
quiz.w: Warranties usually cover manufacturing faults.

quiz.q: How do support tiers usually differ?
quiz.w: Higher tiers often add faster response and replacement.

quiz.q: A hospital cannot tolerate a long outage. What do you suggest?
o: A higher support tier with fast replacement
quiz.w: Critical customers benefit from faster replacement and 24x7 help.

pages.t: RMA means return merchandise authorization. It is the agreed process for returning a product during warranty to get a refund, repair or replacement. You request an RMA before sending anything back.
g: Return merchandise authorization: a permission and number for sending back a faulty product.

pages.t: The RMA gives the vendor a chance to diagnose the problem first. Some 'faulty' products turn out to be setup or configuration issues. So expect questions and tests before an RMA is approved.
g: Find out what is actually wrong.

pages.t: With advance replacement, the vendor sends the replacement before receiving the faulty unit, so the customer is down for less time. Some support tiers offer faster or more secure RMA options. Check what the contract includes.
g: Getting the new unit first, then returning the old one.

quiz.q: When do you request an RMA?
quiz.w: The authorization comes before the return happens.

quiz.q: What is advance replacement?
o: The replacement is sent before the faulty unit arrives
quiz.w: It reduces the customer's downtime.

quiz.q: Why might an RMA be questioned at first?
o: The vendor wants a chance to diagnose and possibly fix the issue first
quiz.w: The RMA is a gatekeeping step that lets the vendor diagnose and possibly fix the issue before a return.

pages.t: Subscriptions and support contracts end on a date. A renewal keeps them going. Missing it can mean lost updates, features or support. Good resellers track renewal dates, because that is repeat business and a service to the customer.
g: Extending a subscription or contract for another period.

pages.t: Co-terming aligns several subscriptions so they all end on the same date. A customer with products bought at different times gets one renewal instead of many. A later purchase is adjusted for the shorter time left.
g: Charging only for the part of the period that remains.

pages.t: Not every vendor or product allows co-terming, and rules on how it is priced differ. Ask the vendor or your distributor before promising it to a customer. A single renewal date simplifies budgeting for the customer.
g: Planning what will be spent and when.

quiz.q: What does co-terming do?
o: Aligns subscriptions to one shared end date
quiz.w: It synchronises end dates so there is one renewal.

quiz.q: A customer added a licence in April, other licences renew in January. What does co-terming help with?
o: Aligning the April licence to the January renewal, with adjusted cost
Moving the January renewal to April only
quiz.w: The newer item is prorated so it ends with the others.

quiz.q: What should you do before promising co-terming?
o: Check that the vendor supports it
quiz.w: Co-terming rules differ between vendors.

pages.t: A cloud-managed product is configured and monitored through a web portal run by the vendor. The provider runs the platform and handles its updates, so the customer does not host the management software.
g: Controlled through a vendor-hosted web portal.
A website where you manage your devices or account.

pages.t: Cloud management is often a subscription, sold per device or per feature, and terms differ by vendor. Check what is free, what needs a subscription and what happens to the device if it ends. In some products the device stops working after a grace period.

Many sites can be seen from one dashboard, so MSPs and multi-site customers save visits. The trade-off is dependence on the vendor's cloud and a recurring cost. Offer on-premises options where the customer cannot use cloud.
g: Software run on the customer's own server instead of in the cloud.

quiz.q: Who runs the management platform in a cloud-managed product?
quiz.w: The provider operates the platform and updates it.

quiz.q: Which customer benefits most from cloud management?
o: A single home user with one device
A company with many remote sites
A site with no internet at all
quiz.w: One dashboard saves visits across many sites.

quiz.q: What should you clarify when quoting?
o: What is free, what needs a subscription, and what happens when it ends
quiz.w: Terms vary and surprises hurt trust.

pages.t: A SKU identifies one exact item for sale, such as a model in a certain colour or pack size. Codes are not standardised, so a vendor's part number and a distributor's SKU can differ. Always quote the exact code to avoid mistakes.
g: Stock keeping unit: a code for one specific item.
The manufacturer's code for a product.

pages.t: Stock is what the distributor holds now. Lead time is the delay from order to delivery. Items in stock ship fast. Items not in stock must be ordered from the vendor, with a lead time that can change.
g: How many units can ship right away.
The wait between ordering and receiving.

pages.t: Tell the customer the realistic date, not the hope. For projects, check stock early, order in time, and ask about backorders or alternatives. Do not confirm delivery to the customer before you have it from your distributor.
g: An order placed for something that is out of stock and will come later.

quiz.q: What does a SKU identify?
quiz.w: A SKU is a code for a distinct item.

quiz.q: What is lead time?
o: The wait between order and delivery
quiz.w: It is the delay from ordering to receiving.

quiz.q: A customer needs 30 units for a project in three weeks, none in stock. What do you do?
o: Check stock and lead time early and order promptly
quiz.w: Realistic dates and early orders prevent trouble.

lessons.title: NFR units, deal registration and margin words

pages.t: NFR means not for resale. Vendors give partners such units or licences for testing, demos and training, not to sell on. They may be limited to the partner's own office or banned from production use. Terms differ by vendor.
g: Not for resale: for the partner's own use, not to be sold.
A unit used to show a product to customers.

pages.t: In deal registration a partner tells the vendor about a specific opportunity. If approved, the partner gets protection for a set period, so another partner or the vendor's own team does not step in. Vendors differ on the rules and how long protection lasts.
g: A potential sale being worked on.
All the opportunities a seller is working.

pages.t: List price is the vendor's published price. Discount is the reduction from list. Margin is what the seller keeps after the cost of goods. Vendors may offer better terms for registered deals. Partner terms are usually confidential, so never share them.
g: The difference between what you pay and what you sell for.
The official starting price before discounts.

quiz.q: What is an NFR unit for?
quiz.w: NFR means not for resale and is for the partner's own evaluation.

quiz.q: What does deal registration give a partner?
o: Protection on a specific opportunity for a set time
quiz.w: Approved registrations protect the partner's work.

quiz.q: What is margin?
o: The seller's gain after the cost of goods
quiz.w: Margin is what the seller keeps.

quiz.q: A reseller asks what another reseller pays. What do you do?
quiz.w: Partner terms are normally confidential between vendor and partner.

lessons.title: End of sale and end of life

src.l: HPE Networking end of life information

pages.t: End of sale (EoS) is the date after which a product can no longer be ordered. End of life (EoL) is the process of retiring it. The last date of support is when support under contract ends.
g: End of sale: last day to order.
End of life: the process of retiring a product.

pages.t: Vendors such as Cisco and HPE announce end of sale in advance, then keep supporting active contracts for a period afterwards. Some, like Cisco, stop selling support or subscriptions that would run past the last support date. Each vendor sets its own periods and names.
g: The public notice of EoS and EoL dates.

pages.t: Customers on old products need a migration plan. EoS is a chance to propose a successor, not a crisis. Check lifecycle dates before quoting a long-term project, so you do not sell something about to be retired.
g: Moving from an old product to a new one.
The newer product that replaces an older one.

quiz.q: What does end of sale mean?
o: The product can no longer be ordered
quiz.w: EoS is the last date to order.

quiz.q: After end of sale, what usually continues for a while?
quiz.w: Vendors such as Cisco and HPE keep supporting active contracts for a limited time after end of sale.

quiz.q: You are quoting a 5 year project. What should you check?
quiz.w: A soon-to-retire product is a poor basis for a long project.
